proposal.name: Work on several issues at once

plan.name: Work on several issues at once
plan.summary: The watcher runs up to `-parallel N` steps at once, 3 by default, one per issue (D-0113): with Factory.Parallel above 1, Poll starts a step on each open issue that has none running, in order of number, waits for a free slot whenever N are running, and returns without waiting for its steps, so steps run across polls and each step's error is logged as it ends; Wait waits until none is running, and `watch -once` polls and then waits. With Parallel 0 or 1, Poll takes one step at a time and returns once they've ended, as the watcher does today, and either way it reads each issue again just before its step (the GitHub interface gains Issue, as github.Client has it) and skips one that's been closed. Everything steps share is safe from several at once: every call on the watcher's clone, from a step or the lease, runs alone, so no two git commands overlap and one step's saved result can't take in another's; the cache of who can write takes a lock; and Watch clears the clone's worktrees once, the first time it may act, before it starts any step, instead of before each poll. Losing the lease stops every running step before its next effect and drops its agent run, as it does one now, and Steps lists each running step's issue, what it's doing and since when, which the watcher writes to its status file as steps on every change, keeping its single issue and step as the longest-running one for the page as it is. Left for a follow-up issue: the dashboard reading that list and showing each step live.

tests.name: TestAnotherIssueIsAnsweredDuringABuild
tests.says: While #1's build is held open, the same poll drafts #2 and posts its proposal; once the build is let go, #1 gets its pull request.

tests.name: TestAStepNeverStartsTwiceOnOneIssue
tests.says: Polls return while #1's build is held open and start nothing more on #1: it builds once, and its only new post is its pull request.

tests.name: TestLosingTheLeaseStopsEveryStep
tests.says: When another watcher takes the lease while #1 builds and #2 drafts, both steps stop before their next effect: no post, label, push or pull request, and both runs stay recorded with no result.

tests.name: TestNoMoreStepsRunThanParallel
tests.says: With two at most, a poll starts #1 and #2, waits for one to end, skips #3, closed while it waited, and starts #4; no more than two drafts ever run at once.

tests.name: TestAnIssueClosedDuringAPollGetsNoStep
tests.says: With -parallel 1, one step at a time as today, an issue closed while an earlier issue built gets no draft and no post from the same poll.

tests.name: TestPollsKeepARunningStepsWorktree
tests.says: While Watch keeps polling during #1's held build, no poll clears the build's worktree, and the build ends in a pull request.

tests.name: TestStepsListsEveryRunningStep
tests.says: While #1 builds and #2 drafts, Steps lists each once, with what it's doing and since when, and lists nothing once both end.

tests.name: TestTwoDraftsAtOnceKeepTheirOwnRecords
tests.says: Two drafts that end at the same moment each record their own result, not the other's.

tests.name: TestTwoIssuesAtOnceSurviveACrashAnywhere
tests.says: Stopping the watcher before any effect of two issues whose steps run at once, then starting a fresh one on the same machine or another, merges both with every effect done once.

tests.name: TestTheStatusListsEveryStep
tests.says: The watcher's status file holds a list of steps, each with its issue, what it's doing and since when, and reads back the same.

usage.summary:
The check passed on the first try. It confirmed that all 10 acceptance tests fail on the current code and that the change touches the trusted base, so a person merges it. The plan covers the watcher's side of #107: `-parallel N` (3 by default) runs one step per issue, polls return while steps keep running, every call on the clone runs alone, each issue is read again before its step, worktrees are cleared once instead of before every poll, losing the lease stops every step, and a `Steps` list goes into the status file; the dashboard reading that list and showing each step live is left for a follow-up issue.

I couldn't compile the tests here, and the check doesn't prove they compile against the new API. They fail now because that API doesn't exist yet, which also means a slip on my side wouldn't show until the build. I checked the gofmt formatting and vet rules by hand, since the build can't edit the test files.
